audit.whatIsWrong: The full-layer level chart disagreed with the content layer on 6 of 7 rows, so the page rendered two different answers to 'who wins Level 1'.
audit.why: packet.levelChart (Skill, Skill, Ahri, Ahri, Malzahar, Ahri, Skill) matches content win[0..6] and whys[0..6]; the full layer carried a different set of sides entirely.
audit.corrected: phases[N].side moved to match win[N] on rows 0-5, with each why rewritten to argue the new verdict. Row 6 already agreed.

audit.whatIsWrong: Spikes prose was fine, but phases[4] and phases[5] argued the wrong owner of the spike.
audit.why: Level 6 is Malzahar's: Nether Grasp is point-and-click suppression on a 12s Charm cooldown window. First item is Ahri's: Spirit Rush gives three dashes to leave the 700 R range.
audit.corrected: phases[4] -> Malzahar naming Charm's flat 12s; phases[5] -> Ahri naming the three dashes vs 700 R range.

audit.whatIsWrong: Ahri was described as having a shield ('poke his shield off', 'the purple bubble', 'spell shield (Iron Boundary)'). Ahri has no shield, and 'Iron Boundary' is not a Malzahar ability.
audit.why: ownerKit P is Void Shift-style damage reduction plus CC immunity that lapses on damage taken; enemyKit has no shield in any slot. Ahri's Q returns as true damage, so stacking MR is the wrong answer — this was absent from the page entirely.
audit.corrected: Every 'shield' reference re-pointed at Malzahar's own passive; tradeBad now states the true-damage return; Essence Theft's per-9-minion heal added to breakdown.mid as the anti-heal note.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns contained no digit at all (lint COOLDOWN_NO_DIGIT).
audit.why: It is the one field that exists to hold real numbers.
audit.corrected: Charm 12s flat, Fox-Fire 9s to 5s across ranks, Nether Grasp 140/110/80.

audit.whatIsWrong: Two Do's/Don'ts bodies were the tradeGood/tradeBad strings pasted under unrelated titles (lint COPY_PASTE_BLEED), and ten fields called Ahri 'he/his/him'.
audit.corrected: All flagged pronouns fixed; dosFull[1].d and dontsFull[2].d rewritten to match their own titles.

audit.whatIsWrong: packet flagged wants.foe[1] 'Use Spirit Rush' as a probable wrong ability name.
audit.why: Spirit Rush is Ahri's real R in enemyKit. False positive.

edits.before: Liandry's spike: visions melt waves AND health bars. Suppress-into-burn kills through most defensive answers.
edits.after: Her spike: Spirit Rush's three dashes dodge your Q and leave 700 R range. Liandry's burn only lands on a caught Ahri.

edits.before: His combo through a broken shield kills you — so the shield is the matchup. Guard it like a third summoner.
edits.after: Her Charm into Orb kills you once Void Shift is stripped — so Void Shift is the matchup. Guard it like a summoner.

edits.before: Ahri wins by landing Charm, denying your pattern, and keeping the fight at a distance your kit resents.
edits.after: Ahri wins by landing Charm at 975 range, then Orb and Fox-Fire, and by dashing outside your 700 R.

edits.before: Pop-and-punish: poke his shield off with a cheap E-tick, then Q-W-E the gap before it rebuilds — full rotations only ever land on shieldless targets.
edits.after: Punish the whiff: when Charm misses she is defenceless for 12 seconds — E her, Q to silence Fox-Fire, and let voidlings finish while Void Shift holds.

edits.before: Trading into him with YOUR shield down — you are the squishiest scaling mage in the pool the moment the purple bubble disappears.
edits.after: Trading with Void Shift already broken — her Q returns as true damage, so no amount of MR saves you once Charm connects.

edits.before: - Ahri Charm: matchup-defining — The charm starts every kill pattern — stay behind minions while it is up. Check it before every step-up. - spell shield (Iron Boundary) is the lifeline; chip damage never gets it. - The ult answers fights, not waves.
edits.after: - Charm (E) is a flat 12s at every rank — that window is your green light. - Fox-Fire drops from 9s to 5s by rank 5, so late-lane poke never stops. - Void Shift needs you undamaged; chip breaks it. - Nether Grasp is 140/110/80s: spend it on her, not a wave.

edits.before: Set the metronome: E the wave, shield-manage the poke, and silence only what matters. You are not dueling anyone — you are billing them for tempo.
edits.after: Set the metronome: E the wave, keep Void Shift intact vs Orb poke, and save Q's silence for Charm. You are not dueling her — you are billing her for tempo.

edits.before: Post-6 every lane state includes the Grasp threat: shove, ward, and punish anyone who walks into point-and-click range. With a jungler nearby, your R is a written guarantee.
edits.after: Post-6 every lane state includes the Grasp threat: shove, ward, and punish any step into 700 range. Essence Theft heals her every 9 minions, so Liandry's chip alone never wins.

notes: Chart: the content layer (win[] and whys[]) already matched packet.levelChart exactly, so all six chart edits are full-layer side+why pairs with no win[N] edit — win[N] was already the target value and a no-op edit would take the group down. phases[N].rating left untouched: the ratings read as per-stage difficulty for the owner and nothing in the brief tells me the scale, so I did not want to guess and break a group. The page repeatedly described Ahri as having a spell shield ('the purple bubble', 'shieldless targets') and named it 'Iron Boundary' — neither champion has that ability; I re-pointed every reference at Malzahar's own passive (Void Shift). packet suspectName wants.foe[1] 'Use Spirit Rush' is a FALSE POSITIVE — Spirit Rush is Ahri's real R. Left alone as templated but true: 'ahead' and breakdown.spikes/feeding, which already name Ahri specifics.
